entities.name: Green Revolution
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary: The introduction of high-yielding crop varieties, irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides to developing countries (1950s–1970s), led by Norman Borlaug. Wheat yields in Mexico tripled; India went from famine to self-sufficiency in grain. The revolution saved an estimated billion lives but raised concerns about environmental sustainability and rural inequality.

entities.name: Green Revolution
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat varieties doubled and tripled yields in Mexico, India, and Pakistan. Combined with fertilizers and irrigation, the Green Revolution averted predicted mass famines.
